key_insight: Detonation-sprayed titanium dioxide-based coatings can be tuned for roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity by adjusting process parameters such as nozzle speed and spray distance.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical process-property relationships and fitted equations that can guide optimization of coating performance in surface engineering applications.
method: Varied detonation spraying parameters under different process conditions.
Measured coating surface roughness, thickness, and contact angle (hydrophobicity).
Derived empirical laws linking nozzle speed and spray distance to surface properties.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parameter-dependent trends and new predictive equations, including inverse power-law behavior for roughness/thickness versus nozzle speed and parabolic dependence of roughness/contact angle on spray distance.
watch_item: The relationships appear empirical and process-specific, so transferability to other materials, equipment, or operating windows may require additional validation.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
